ukberi-tibyan:195-195.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (بِلِسَانٍ عَرَبِيٍّ مُبِينٍ (١٩٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِلِسَانٍ): the bāʾ may be attached to (mutaʿalliq) الْمُنْذِرِينَ, and it may be a badal (substitute) from «بِهِ», i.e. "he brought it down in a clear Arabic tongue", that is, with a message, or a language.

ukberi-tibyan:197-197.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَوَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُمْ آيَةً أَنْ يَعْلَمَهُ عُلَمَاءُ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ (١٩٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَوَلَمْ يَكُنْ): it is read with tāʾ (تكن), and in it there are two views. The first: it is the complete (tāmma) [kāna], the fāʿil (agent) is «آيَةٌ», and «أَنْ يَعْلَمَهُ» is a badal (substitute), or the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); i.e. "has there not come about for them a sign?" The second: it is the deficient (nāqiṣa) [kāna], and concerning its noun there are two views. One of them: it is the pronoun of the story (ḍamīr al-qiṣṣa), «أَنْ يَعْلَمَهُ» is a mubtadaʾ, «آيَةً» is a fronted khabar, and the clause is the khabar of kāna. The second: its noun is «آيَةٌ», and concerning the khabar there are two views. One of them: [the khabar is] «لَهُمْ», and «أَنْ يَعْلَمَهُ» is a badal, or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ.
The second: [the khabar is] «أَنْ يَعْلَمَهُ».
It is permissible for the khabar to be definite here because the indefiniteness and definiteness of the maṣdar (verbal noun) are the same, and «آيَةً» has been specified by «لَهُمْ», and because no particular [instance] is intended by the knowledge of the Children of Israel.
It is also read with yāʾ (يكن); so it may be like [the reading with] tāʾ, because the feminine gender is not real.
And with yāʾ it has also been read with آيَةً in the accusative (naṣb), on the basis that it is a fronted khabar.

ukberi-tibyan:198-198.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَوْ نَزَّلْنَاهُ عَلَى بَعْضِ الْأَعْجَمِينَ (١٩٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الْأَعْجَمِينَ): i.e. الْأَعْجَمِيِّينَ, the yāʾ of relation (yāʾ al-nisba) having been omitted, just as they said الْأَشْعَرُونَ, meaning الْأَشْعَرِيُّونَ. Its singular is أَعْجَمِيٌّ. It cannot be the plural of أَعْجَمُ, because its feminine is عَجْمَاءُ, and a word like this is not given the sound plural.

ukberi-tibyan:200-200.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (كَذَلِكَ سَلَكْنَاهُ فِي قُلُوبِ الْمُجْرِمِينَ (٢٠٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (سَلَكْنَاهُ): its like has been mentioned in [Sūrat] al-Ḥijr. And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:202-203.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَيَأْتِيَهُمْ بَغْتَةً وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ (٢٠٢) فَيَقُولُوا هَلْ نَحْنُ مُنْظَرُونَ (٢٠٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَيَأْتِيَهُمْ), (فَيَقُولُوا): both are maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «يَرَوْا».

ukberi-tibyan:207-207.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (مَا أَغْنَى عَنْهُمْ مَا كَانُوا يُمَتَّعُونَ (٢٠٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَا أَغْنَى عَنْهُمْ): it may be an interrogative, in which case «مَا» is in the position of the accusative; and it may be a negation, i.e. "it did not avail them anything."

ukberi-tibyan:209-209.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (ذِكْرَى وَمَا كُنَّا ظَالِمِينَ (٢٠٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (ذِكْرَى): it may be a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), and it may be the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "the warning is a reminder."

ukberi-tibyan:223-223.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يُلْقُونَ السَّمْعَ وَأَكْثَرُهُمْ كَاذِبُونَ (٢٢٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يُلْقُونَ): it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) in «تَنَزَّلُ».

ukberi-tibyan:225-225.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّهُمْ فِي كُلِّ وَادٍ يَهِيمُونَ (٢٢٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَهِيمُونَ): it may be the khabar (predicate) of «أَنَّ», and so it governs «فِي كُلِّ وَادٍ»; and it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial), in which case the khabar is «فِي كُلِّ وَادٍ».
Allah the Exalted says: (إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ وَذَكَرُوا اللَّهَ كَثِيرًا وَانْتَصَرُوا مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا ظُلِمُوا وَسَيَعْلَمُ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا أَيَّ مُنْقَلَبٍ يَنْقَلِبُونَ (٢٢٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَيَّ مُنْقَلَبٍ): it is an adjective (ṣifa) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), and its operator is «يَنْقَلِبُونَ», i.e. "they will turn with a turning, whatever turning [it be]." «يُعْلَمُ» [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has سَيَعْلَمُ.] does not govern it, because what precedes an interrogative does not govern it. And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:1-3.t: Allah the Exalted says: (طسم (١) تِلْكَ آيَاتُ الْكِتَابِ الْمُبِينِ (٢) لَعَلَّكَ بَاخِعٌ نَفْسَكَ أَلَّا يَكُونُوا مُؤْمِنِينَ (٣)). (طسم): like الم, and it was mentioned at the beginning of al-Baqara. (تِلْكَ آيَاتُ الْكِتَابِ): like ذَلِكَ الْكِتَابُ. And (أَنْ لَا يَكُونُوا) is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "so that not" (لِئَلَّا), or "for fear that not" (مَخَافَةَ أَنْ لَا).

ukberi-tibyan:4-4.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنْ نَشَأْ نُنَزِّلْ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ آيَةً فَظَلَّتْ أَعْنَاقُهُمْ لَهَا خَاضِعِينَ (٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَظَلَّتْ), i.e. "and then would remain" (فَتَظَلُّ); its position is jussive (majzūm), conjoined to the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). It may also be nominative, as resumptive.
His saying, Exalted is He: (خَاضِعِينَ): it is put in the masculine plural for four reasons. The first: what is meant by الأعناق ("the necks") is their great men. The second: He meant the owners of their necks. The third: it is the plural of عُنُق in the sense of a group of people, so it means the groups, not the necks. The fourth: since He annexed الأعناق to a masculine [rational] noun, and they are joined to them in their physical make-up, He applied to them the rule that applies to their owners.
Al-Kisāʾī said: «خَاضِعِينَ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) belonging to the genitive pronoun, not to الأعناق. On close examination this is far-fetched, because «خَاضِعِينَ» would then be predicated of something other than the agent of ظلّت, so it would require the agent pronoun to be made overt; it would have had to be: خَاضِعِينَ هُمْ.

ukberi-tibyan:7-7.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا إِلَى الْأَرْضِ كَمْ أَنْبَتْنَا فِيهَا مِنْ كُلِّ زَوْجٍ كَرِيمٍ (٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كَمْ): in the position of the accusative, governed by «أَنْبَتْنَا». And «مِنْ كُلِّ» is a tamyīz (specification); it may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial).

ukberi-tibyan:10-10.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِذْ نَادَى رَبُّكَ مُوسَى أَنِ ائْتِ الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ (١٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَإِذْ نَادَى), i.e. "and mention when He called" (وَاذْكُرْ إِذْ نَادَى). And (أَنِ ائْتِ): أنْ is maṣdar-forming, or in the sense of أي ("that is", explicative).

ukberi-tibyan:11-11.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَوْمَ فِرْعَوْنَ أَلَا يَتَّقُونَ (١١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (قَوْمَ): it is a badal (substitute) of what precedes it.
(أَلَا يَتَّقُونَ): it is read with yāʾ, as resumptive, and with tāʾ, as direct address; the implied wording [on the latter] is: "O people of Pharaoh" (يَا قَوْمَ فِرْعَوْنَ). It is also said that it [قوم] is the object of يتقون.

ukberi-tibyan:13-13.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَيَضِيقُ صَدْرِي وَلَا يَنْطَلِقُ لِسَانِي فَأَرْسِلْ إِلَى هَارُونَ (١٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَيَضِيقُ صَدْرِي): in the nominative, as resumptive, i.e. "and I – my breast is constricted by the denial"; and in the accusative, conjoined to the accusative verb before it. Likewise (يَنْطَلِقُ).
(فَأَرْسِلْ إِلَى هَارُونَ), i.e. "an angel to inform him that he is my support", or "a prophet with me".

ukberi-tibyan:16-16.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَأْتِيَا فِرْعَوْنَ فَقُولَا إِنَّا رَسُولُ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ (١٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِنَّا رَسُولُ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ): there are several views on its being singular. The first: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), like الرسالة ("the message"), i.e. "bearers of a message" (ذَوَا رَسُولٍ), or "we are a message", by way of hyperbole. The second: it makes do with one of the two, since they were both on one mission. The third: Moses, peace be upon him, was the principal and Aaron a follower, so He mentioned the principal.

ukberi-tibyan:18-19.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ أَلَمْ نُرَبِّكَ فِينَا وَلِيدًا وَلَبِثْتَ فِينَا مِنْ عُمُرِكَ سِنِينَ (١٨) وَفَعَلْتَ فَعْلَتَكَ الَّتِي فَعَلْتَ وَأَنْتَ مِنَ الْكَافِرِينَ (١٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ عُمُرِكَ): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «سِنِينَ».
And (فَعْلَتَكَ) is with fatḥa; it has also been read with kasra, i.e. "[the manner of doing] customary with you".

ukberi-tibyan:22-22.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَتِلْكَ نِعْمَةٌ تَمُنُّهَا عَلَيَّ أَنْ عَبَّدْتَ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ (٢٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَتِلْكَ): the interrogative particle is omitted, i.e. "and is that…?" (أَوَتِلْكَ).
And (تَمُنُّهَا) is in the position of the nominative as an adjective of نعمة; the preposition is omitted, i.e. "with which [you reproach me]" (بِهَا). It is also said: «عَلَيَّ» is construed with ذِكْر or with عَبْد. [Translator's note: so in the source («حُمِلَ عَلَيَّ بِذِكْرٍ أَوْ بِعَبْدٍ»); the intended sense is unclear, and it may be corrupt.]
And (أَنْ عَبَّدْتَ) is a badal (substitute) of نعمة; or it is on the implied "it is" (هِيَ); or a badal of the hāʾ in تمنّها; or in the position of the genitive with the bāʾ implied, i.e. "in that you enslaved" (بِأَنْ عَبَّدْتَ).

ukberi-tibyan:23-24.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ فِرْعَوْنُ وَمَا رَبُّ الْعَالَمِينَ (٢٣) قَالَ رَبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُوقِنِينَ (٢٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمَا رَبُّ الْعَالَمِينَ): he used «مَا» only because he was asking about His attributes and acts, i.e. "what are His attributes and what are His acts?" Had he meant His essence, he would have said مَن ("who"); for that reason Moses, peace be upon him, answered him with his words: «رَبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ».
It is also said: he was ignorant of what the question really was, so Moses brought the real answer.

ukberi-tibyan:34-34.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ لِلْمَلَأِ حَوْلَهُ إِنَّ هَذَا لَسَاحِرٌ عَلِيمٌ (٣٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لِلْمَلَإِ حَوْلَهُ): [حوله is] a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الملأ, i.e. "being around him".
The Kufans said: the qualified noun is omitted, i.e. "those who were around him" (الَّذِينَ حَوْلَهُ). There are many questions here which were mentioned in al-Aʿrāf and Ṭā Hā.

ukberi-tibyan:44-44.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَأَلْقَوْا حِبَالَهُمْ وَعِصِيَّهُمْ وَقَالُوا بِعِزَّةِ فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّا لَنَحْنُ الْغَالِبُونَ (٤٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِعِزَّةِ فِرْعَوْنَ), i.e. "we swear" (نَحْلِفُ).

ukberi-tibyan:51-51.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّا نَطْمَعُ أَنْ يَغْفِرَ لَنَا رَبُّنَا خَطَايَانَا أَنْ كُنَّا أَوَّلَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ (٥١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنْ كُنَّا), i.e. "because we were" (لِأَنْ كُنَّا).

ukberi-tibyan:54-56.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّ هَؤُلَاءِ لَشِرْذِمَةٌ قَلِيلُونَ (٥٤) وَإِنَّهُمْ لَنَا لَغَائِظُونَ (٥٥) وَإِنَّا لَجَمِيعٌ حَاذِرُونَ (٥٦))
His saying, Exalted is He: (قَلِيلُونَ): put in the plural according to the meaning, because الشرذمة ("the band") is a group.
And (حَذِرُونَ), without alif, and with alif, are two dialectal forms. It is also said: الحاذر, with alif, is the one who is armed. It is also read with dāl [حَادِرُونَ]; الحادر is the strong one, and also the one filled with rage or fear.

ukberi-tibyan:59-59.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (كَذَلِكَ وَأَوْرَثْنَاهَا بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ (٥٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كَذَلِكَ), i.e. "a bringing out like that" (إِخْرَاجًا كَذَلِكَ).

ukberi-tibyan:60-60.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَأَتْبَعُوهُمْ مُشْرِقِينَ (٦٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مُشْرِقِينَ): a ḥāl (circumstantial). المُشرِق is the one upon whom sunrise has come.

ukberi-tibyan:61-61.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَلَمَّا تَرَاءَى الْجَمْعَانِ قَالَ أَصْحَابُ مُوسَى إِنَّا لَمُدْرَكُونَ (٦١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَمُدْرَكُونَ), without doubling and with doubling; one says أَدْرَكْتُهُ and ادَّرَكْتُهُ ("I overtook him").

ukberi-tibyan:64-64.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَأَزْلَفْنَا ثَمَّ الْآخَرِينَ (٦٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَأَزْلَفْنَا): with fāʾ, i.e. "We brought near"; the reference is to the companions of Moses.
It is also read, irregularly (shādhdh), with qāf [وَأَزْلَقْنَا], i.e. "We brought the people of Pharaoh to a slippery place".

ukberi-tibyan:70-70.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِذْ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِ مَا تَعْبُدُونَ (٧٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذْ قَالَ): what governs إذ is «نَبَأَ» [Translator's note: the source has «نَبَّأَ»; the word in the preceding verse is نَبَأَ, "the story".].

ukberi-tibyan:72-72.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ هَلْ يَسْمَعُونَكُمْ إِذْ تَدْعُونَ (٧٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (هَلْ يَسْمَعُونَكُمْ): it is read with fatḥa on the yāʾ and on the mīm, i.e. "do they hear your calling?" (يَسْمَعُونَ دُعَاءَكُمْ); the muḍāf was omitted because «تَدْعُونَ» indicates it.
It is also read with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the mīm, i.e. "do they make you hear the answer to your calling upon them?"

ukberi-tibyan:74-74.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالُوا بَلْ وَجَدْنَا آبَاءَنَا كَذَلِكَ يَفْعَلُونَ (٧٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كَذَلِكَ): accusative, governed by «يَفْعَلُونَ».

ukberi-tibyan:77-77.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَإِنَّهُمْ عَدُوٌّ لِي إِلَّا رَبَّ الْعَالَمِينَ (٧٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَإِنَّهُمْ عَدُوٌّ لِي): it is put in the singular as denoting a relation (ʿalā al-nasab), i.e. "people of enmity"; for that reason one says of a feminine: هِيَ عَدُوٌّ, just as one says حائض ("menstruating", without the feminine ending); but عَدُوَّةٌ has also been heard.
(إِلَّا رَبَّ الْعَالَمِينَ): there are two views on it. The first: it is an exception from a different genus (disjunctive), because He is not included in the number [of the enemies]. The second: it is from the same genus, because among their forefathers there were those who worshipped Allah and others besides Allah. And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:78-78.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (الَّذِي خَلَقَنِي فَهُوَ يَهْدِينِ (٧٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الَّذِي خَلَقَنِي): «الَّذِي» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), «فَهُوَ» a second mubtadaʾ, and «يَهْدِينِي» its khabar (predicate); the clause is the khabar of «الَّذِي».
As for the occurrences of «الَّذِي» after it, they are adjectives of the first الذي; the wāw may be brought in between adjectives. It is also said that what is conjoined is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, being dispensed with by the khabar of the first.

ukberi-tibyan:85-85.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَاجْعَلْنِي مِنْ وَرَثَةِ جَنَّةِ النَّعِيمِ (٨٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَاجْعَلْنِي مِنْ وَرَثَةِ), i.e. "an heir from among the heirs of…" (وَارِثًا مِنْ وَرَثَةِ…); so من is attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted.

ukberi-tibyan:87-89.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَا تُخْزِنِي يَوْمَ يُبْعَثُونَ (٨٧) يَوْمَ لَا يَنْفَعُ مَالٌ وَلَا بَنُونَ (٨٨) إِلَّا مَنْ أَتَى اللَّهَ بِقَلْبٍ سَلِيمٍ (٨٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَوْمَ لَا يَنْفَعُ): it is a badal (substitute) of the first «يَوْمَ».
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِلَّا مَنْ أَتَى اللَّهَ): there are two views on it. The first: it is from a different genus (disjunctive), i.e. "but whoever comes to Allah… will be safe" or "will benefit".
The second: it is connected (muttaṣil); and in this there are two views. The first: it is in the position of the accusative, as a badal of the omitted [object], or as an exception from it; the implied wording is: "neither wealth nor sons will benefit anyone, except whoever comes…" (لَا يَنْفَعُ مَالٌ وَلَا بَنُونَ أَحَدًا إِلَّا مَنْ أَتَى). The meaning is that when wealth is spent in the ways of righteousness, and [in the case of] righteous sons, the one connected to them and to their righteousness benefits from them. The second view: it is in the position of the nominative as a badal of the agent of ينفع, the rational being given precedence; the implied wording is then: "except the wealth of whoever…" or "the sons of whoever…", for that benefits himself or others through intercession.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: it may be the object of ينفع, i.e. "that benefits no one except a man who comes to Allah".

ukberi-tibyan:98-98.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِذْ نُسَوِّيكُمْ بِرَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ (٩٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذْ نُسَوِّيكُمْ): what governs it may be «مُبِينٌ», or an omitted verb indicated by «ضَلَالٌ»; ضلال cannot govern it, because it has been qualified by an adjective.

ukberi-tibyan:102-102.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَلَوْ أَنَّ لَنَا كَرَّةً فَنَكُونَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ (١٠٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَنَكُونَ): it is conjoined to «كَرَّةً», i.e. "if only we could return and be", that is, "and that we be" (فَأَنْ نَكُونَ).

ukberi-tibyan:111-111.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالُوا أَنُؤْمِنُ لَكَ وَاتَّبَعَكَ الْأَرْذَلُونَ (١١١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَاتَّبَعَكَ): the wāw is circumstantial (wāw al-ḥāl).
It has been read irregularly (shādhdh) «وَأَتْبَاعُكَ» ("and your followers"), as a plural; there are two views on it:
The first: it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and what follows is the khabar (predicate), the clause being a ḥāl (circumstantial).
The second: it is conjoined to the agent pronoun in «نُؤْمِنُ», and (الْأَرْذَلُونَ) is an adjective, i.e. "are we and they to be equal?"

ukberi-tibyan:118-118.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَافْتَحْ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَهُمْ فَتْحًا وَنَجِّنِي وَمَنْ مَعِيَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ (١١٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَتْحًا): it may be an emphatic maṣdar (verbal noun), and it may be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), الفتح then meaning "what is opened (judged)", as they said: "this is among the conquests (فتوح) of ʿUmar".

ukberi-tibyan:128-129.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَتَبْنُونَ بِكُلِّ رِيعٍ آيَةً تَعْبَثُونَ (١٢٨) وَتَتَّخِذُونَ مَصَانِعَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَخْلُدُونَ (١٢٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (تَعْبَثُونَ): it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «تَبْنُونَ».
And (تَخْلُدُونَ) is read in the active voice without doubling, and in the passive both with doubling and without it; the past is خلد and أخلد.

ukberi-tibyan:132-133.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَاتَّقُوا الَّذِي أَمَدَّكُمْ بِمَا تَعْلَمُونَ (١٣٢) أَمَدَّكُمْ بِأَنْعَامٍ وَبَنِينَ (١٣٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَمَدَّكُمْ بِأَنْعَامٍ): this clause is explicative of what precedes it, and it has no grammatical position.

ukberi-tibyan:136-137.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالُوا سَوَاءٌ عَلَيْنَا أَوَعَظْتَ أَمْ لَمْ تَكُنْ مِنَ الْوَاعِظِينَ (١٣٦) إِنْ هَذَا إِلَّا خُلُقُ الْأَوَّلِينَ (١٣٧))
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَمْ لَمْ تَكُنْ مِنَ الْوَاعِظِينَ): this clause stands in the place of "or did not admonish" (أَمْ لَمْ تَعِظْ).
(إِنْ هَذَا إِلَّا خُلُقُ): with fatḥa on the khāʾ and sukūn on the lām [خَلْقُ], i.e. "the fabrication of the ancients", that is, like their fabrication.
It may also mean the people [created], i.e. "are we and you anything but like those who came before, in claiming messengership and in denial, and we die and are not brought back?"
It is also read with two ḍammas [خُلُقُ], i.e. "the custom of the ancients".

ukberi-tibyan:146-147.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَتَتْرُكُونَ فِي مَا هَاهُنَا آمِنِينَ (١٤٦) فِي جَنَّاتٍ وَعُيُونٍ (١٤٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فِي جَنَّاتٍ): it is a badal (substitute) of His saying «هَاهُنَا», with the preposition repeated.

ukberi-tibyan:149-149.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَتَنْحِتُونَ مِنَ الْجِبَالِ بُيُوتًا فَارِهِينَ (١٤٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَرِهِينَ): it is a ḥāl (circumstantial). It is also read «فَارِهِينَ» with alif; they are two dialectal forms.

ukberi-tibyan:168-168.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ إِنِّي لِعَمَلِكُمْ مِنَ الْقَالِينَ (١٦٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنَ الْقَالِينَ), i.e. "surely one who detests, among those who detest" (لَقَالٍ مِنَ الْقَالِينَ); so «مِنَ» is an adjective of the khabar (predicate), attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted, and the lām [of لعملكم] is attached to the omitted khabar. In this way one escapes placing the ṣila before the relative [i.e. the dependent of the definite participle before it], since if you made «مِنَ الْقَالِينَ» the khabar, you would make it govern «لِعَمَلِكُمْ».

ukberi-tibyan:176-176.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (كَذَّبَ أَصْحَابُ الْأَيْكَةِ الْمُرْسَلِينَ (١٧٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَصْحَابُ الْأَيْكَةِ): it is read with kasra on the tāʾ, with the hamza pronounced fully, and with it lightened by transferring [its vowel to the lām], like الأنثى and الُانثى.
It has also been read «لَيْكَةَ», with a yāʾ after the lām and fatḥa on the tāʾ. This is not sound, since there is no word «لَيْكَةُ» in the language that could be made a proper name; and if it is claimed that the hamza was changed into a lām, that is extremely far-fetched.

ukberi-tibyan:184-184.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَاتَّقُوا الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ وَالْجِبِلَّةَ الْأَوَّلِينَ (١٨٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَالْجِبِلَّةَ): it is read with kasra on the jīm and the bāʾ, and with ḍamma on them, with doubling [of the lām]; they are two dialectal forms.

ukberi-tibyan:192-193.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِنَّهُ لَتَنْزِيلُ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ (١٩٢) نَزَلَ بِهِ الرُّوحُ الْأَمِينُ (١٩٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَإِنَّهُ): the hāʾ is the pronoun of the Qurʾān, though it has not been mentioned.
And التنزيل is in the sense of "what is sent down" (المُنزَل).
(نَزَلَ بِهِ): it is read in the active voice, the agent being «الرُّوحُ الْأَمِينُ», and in the passive with doubling.
It is also read in the active voice with doubling, with «الرُّوحَ» in the accusative, i.e. "Allah sent down Gabriel with the Qurʾān"; and «بِهِ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
